jobs.title: Executive Director - Sacramento Central & Capital YMCA
jobs.description:
We are The Y, an association that values and is made stronger by its diverse people.

Job Description

Under the direction of the Chief Operations Officer, the Executive Director, Downtown YMCAs provide strategic and operational leadership for the Sacramento Central YMCA and Capital YMCA, overseeing the performance, growth, and impact of both branches.

Serving as the executive leader for both locations, this position is responsible for creating an exceptional member experience, leading high-performing teams, driving membership growth and retention, ensuring operational excellence, and strengthening the YMCA's presence within the downtown and midtown Sacramento community.

The Executive Director directly supervises the Capital Y Branch Manager and the Sacramento Central YMCA Member Services Lead while partnering closely with Association Program Directors and leadership to deliver outstanding programs and services.

As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Executive Director contributes to association-wide strategic planning while maintaining primary responsibility for the successful operation of Sacramento Central and Capital YMCA.

Qualifications

Minimum of five (5) years’ experience in a General Manager, Executive Director, Branch Manager, Operations Manager, or Program Director role (or equivalent).
Strong leadership skills with proven ability to supervise multiple teams and locations.
Exceptional customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Demonstrated ability to develop, implement, and monitor standard operating procedures.
Typical requirements within 30 days of hire include completion of:
Child Abuse Prevention for Supervisory Staff
Working with Program Volunteers
CPR
First Aid
AED
Bloodborne Pathogens
New Employee Orientation
Preventing Workplace Violence
Workplace Harassment

Completion of YMCA program-specific and trainer certifications.
Ability to relate effectively to diverse groups of people from all social and economic segments of the community.

Physical Demands

Sufficient strength, agility, and mobility to perform the essential functions of position and to supervise program activities.

Essential Functions

Branch Leadership & Oversight

Provide executive leadership for Sacramento Central YMCA and Capital YMCA.
Establish a culture of exceptional member service, operational excellence, and accountability.
Maintain a visible presence throughout both branches.
Lead branch strategic planning while ensuring alignment with the YMCA mission and strategic plan.
Build strong relationships with members, staff, volunteers, and community partners.
Support annual campaign efforts, sponsorship development, and community engagement initiatives.
Develop, engage, and support an active Branch Advisory Council by recruiting and cultivating volunteer leaders, providing strategic staff leadership, facilitating meaningful engagement, and leveraging council expertise to advance the YMCA's mission and strengthen community partnerships,

Operational Management

Ensure efficient daily operations across both branches.
Maintain high standards for customer service, cleanliness, safety, and facility presentation.
Oversee branch scheduling, facility utilization, and operational planning.
Ensure compliance with YMCA policies, licensing requirements, and risk management standards.
Monitor branch performance through key operational metrics including membership, retention, service quality, and financial performance.
Develop and implement operational improvements that enhance the member experience.

Financial Leadership

Develop and manage branch operating budgets.
Monitor revenue and expense performance.
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency while maintaining exceptional service.
Collaborate with Finance to ensure sound fiscal management.

Staff Leadership

Supervise the Capital YMCA Branch Manager.
Supervise the Sacramento Central Member Services Lead.
Recruit, coach, develop, and evaluate branch leadership staff.
Foster a positive workplace culture built upon accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
Promote professional development and succession planning throughout branch operations.

Team Development & Collaboration

Recruit, supervise, and develop branch leaders and key operational staff to achieve excellence in service and performance.
Partner and collaborate with HR to ensure best practices in hiring, onboarding, and staff engagement.
Model and reinforce a culture of collaboration, inclusion, and member-focused service across all teams.
Promote communication and shared learning between branches to build a unified service delivery approach.

Leadership & Representation

Serve as a key member of the YMCA Senior Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy and execution.
Represent the YMCA of Superior California in community, civic, and professional forums.
Foster partnerships with local organizations, businesses, and leaders that align with YMCA priorities and mission.
Embody and promote the Y’s core values: caring, honesty, respect, and responsibility in all interactions and decisions.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
About ASG

ASG is a New York–headquartered, SEC-registered investment firm with approximately $1.8 billion in assets under management. The firm invests in global innovation across public and private markets, applying institutional-grade rigor, disciplined underwriting, and proprietary data intelligence to identify and invest in category-defining companies.

Role Summary

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the firm’s organizational anchor. This role most deeply embedded across every function, and the force that transforms the CEO’s vision into a platform capable of sustained, compounding growth.
As AUM scales, organizational complexity is inevitable. The COO’s core mandate is to ensure that structure is always ahead of scale: that governance is codified rather than assumed, that systems are more reliable than any individual, and that the platform is architected to support multiple funds and strategies over the long term.
The COO is accountable for three interconnected layers of value creation:
Designing the organizational and governance architecture that enables the firm to grow without losing cohesion;
Building the systems and process infrastructure that turns institutional experience into repeatable, scalable capability; and
Laying the platform foundation that gives the firm compounding structural advantages as it expands.

The COO is the firm’s connective tissue. The stronger and more integrated that tissue, the more efficiently the entire organization performs.

Core Responsibilities

I. Organizational Governance & Structural Design

1. Three-Engine Clarity: Investment | Finance & Risk | Platform

Define authority boundaries, accountability frameworks, and KPIs across Investment, Finance & Risk, and Platform, formally documented in policy and performance structures.
Maintain clean ownership separation while enabling structured cross-engine coordination.
Audit engine effectiveness as the firm grows and adjust governance design proactively.

2. Layered Decision Architecture

Own and optimize the firm's formal governance bodies (IC, Portfolio Review, Operating Committee, Risk & Valuation Committee), ensuring each addresses the right decision tier.
Design escalation paths, pre-meeting preparation standards, and post-meeting accountability mechanisms.
Establish the firm's weekly, monthly, and quarterly operating cadence as a structured rhythm.

3. Modular Organizational Build-Out

Build functional infrastructure around scoped modules (Fund Ops, IR Ops, Portfolio Ops, Operational Systems, Risk & Compliance), each with defined ownership, deliverables, KPIs, and hiring roadmap.
Partner with HR on headcount planning, role design, and leadership development.
Reinforce firm-wide performance management and accountability norms.

II. Systems, Process & Institutional Infrastructure

1. Single Source of Truth

Lead unification of CRM, Portfolio Management, Fund Administration, and Document Management into a consistent operational data layer.
Establish data governance standards; eliminate version conflicts and shadow tracking.
Select and manage technology vendors against defined SLAs.

2. Risk Control Embedded in Process

Design risk controls into workflows as structural safeguards, not compliance afterthoughts.
Implement access permissions, information barriers, vendor risk management, and key-person mitigation.
Ensure Risk & Compliance has codified integration points within Investment, Finance, and IR workflows.

3. Standardized Playbooks & Institutional Memory

Develop replicable playbooks for core workflows (investment process, QBR, LP DD, LP engagement, crisis management).
Capture institutional knowledge in transferable, maintained systems.
stablish documentation standards; treat playbooks as living documents.

4. Critical Path Optimization & Automation

Eliminate friction in high-frequency workflows (legal execution, KYC, fund administration, capital calls) through SOP redesign, tooling, or restructured ownership.
Prioritize automation to compress cycle times and reduce manual handoffs.
Track cycle time reduction as a core performance metric.

III. Platform Scalability & Long-Term Capability

1. Modular Platform Expansion

Ensure each operational module has defined objectives, measurable outputs, KPIs, and a dedicated budget.
Build shared infrastructure to be strategy-agnostic (VC, Growth, PE, Credit) while investment decision-making remains independent.
Resource operational capacity ahead of AUM growth and fund launch milestones.

2. Budget as Capability Investment

Evaluate infrastructure and vendor investments through an explicit ROI framework focused on long-term capability gain.
Set clear boundaries between self-build, licensed software, and outsourced service models.
Maintain a multi-year operational investment roadmap.

3. Multi-Strategy Shared Platform

Architect the platform so new fund vintages, asset classes, or geographies add incremental, not exponential, operational complexity.
Maintain separation between the platform layer and the investment decision layer.
Build integration standards so new strategies can be onboarded with speed and consistency.

4. Incentive Structure & Long-Term Alignment

Collaborate with the CEO and HR on a compensation framework tied to long-term platform health.
Structure incentive triggers around organizational, system, AUM, and operational efficiency milestones rather than solely deal outcomes.

Required Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in operations, infrastructure, or general management at SEC-registered investment firms, asset managers, hedge funds, institutional financial services firms, or high-growth companies.
Demonstrated track record of building or scaling operational platforms, systems, and teams through periods of rapid growth.
Familiarity with the operational infrastructure supporting investment firms, including fund administration, portfolio management systems, CRM platforms, document management, and risk infrastructure, or demonstrated ability to build comparable systems in another context.
Working knowledge of SEC, RIA, and broader regulatory frameworks applicable to U.S. investment advisers.
Proven experience designing governance structures, decision forums, and operating cadences in growing organizations.
Strong systems thinking, ability to translate strategy into documented, scalable processes.
Sound judgment in vendor selection, technology investment, and build-vs-buy decisions.
Outstanding written communication and documentation discipline.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience as a founder, CEO, or COO of a startup or high-growth company, particularly those who have built operating structure, systems, and teams from an early stage.
Prior COO, Head of Operations, or Chief of Staff experience at an investment firm with AUM growth across multiple fund vintages.
Exposure to both public and private market investment operations.
MBA, JD, CPA, or equivalent advanced credential.
Experience supporting multi-jurisdictional operations (including Asia).

Reporting & Scope

Reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer.
Operates as a senior individual contributor and firm-wide platform architect, working through governance forums, functional partnerships, and CEO-delegated authority. The role does not have direct reports at this time; team build-out under the COO’s scope will be considered as the firm scales.
Sits on or chairs the firm’s principal governance committees as designed.

What We Offer

The opportunity to architect the operational foundation of a growing, SEC-registered investment platform.
High-impact role with direct CEO partnership and meaningful influence across firm strategy.
Competitive compensation, including base, performance bonus, and long-term incentive structure tied to platform health.

jobs.title: Chief Philanthropy Officer
jobs.description:
Americans are struggling, democracy is breaking down, and there is one group of people who can, and will, rebuild our society: young leaders. The C&S team works directly with more than 1000 of the nation’s most energized young changemakers—and impacts millions more through our work with 140+ college presidents—to create bold civic solutions that move our communities, workplaces, and campuses forward. In the last twelve months alone, funders have invested $30MM in C&S’s work, and we have only begun to demonstrate how this movement can repair our intensely divided country. As Chief Philanthropy Officer, you will lead C&S into the next era of partnership-driven fundraising with the same out-of-the-box thinking and relentless creative drive that propels our mission forward today.

The nature of philanthropy is changing. As a rush of new capital enters the ecosystem—from the long-predicted wave of generational wealth transfer to the boom in wealth creation spurred by tech sector IPOs—C&S sees a strategic opportunity to help new philanthropists connect their passions and ambitions to our mission. We have experience partnering with significant donors and institutional foundations on strategy and fund generation for our major projects while also building a base of recurring annual fund donors. Your challenge is to envision and execute a philanthropic strategy that combines our approach to traditional philanthropy with fresh, highly relational, and innovative methods that engage and energize nontraditional donors to leave their mark on the rebuilding of American civil society. We don’t want to limit you with a prescription for what that looks like. We want to partner with you to create it.

How You’ll Make an Impact
With a curious mindset, an uncompromising belief in our mission, and the vision to see opportunity in every conversation, you will work alongside and leverage the talents of capable and energetic fundraising colleagues to help a new generation of philanthropists put their wealth, influence, and ideas to work to change the direction of our nation’s civic future. Key focus areas include:
Prospecting & Prioritization. Build C&S’s presence in circles where opportunity exists, identify and gain the attention of high-capacity prospects, and prioritize and invest deeply in relationships with the most partnership potential.
Relationship Building & Cultivation. Develop donor-centric relationships with emerging philanthropists, learn their interests, motivations, and what keeps them up at night, and bring them into the C&S network.
Philanthropic Advising & Co-Creation. Help emerging philanthropists define the impact they want to achieve and co-create mission-aligned opportunities. Introduce our President, C&S leaders, and other experts in the field at the right moments to move partnerships forward.
Team Leadership & Collaboration. Oversee and partner closely with a strong development team, set strategic direction and ensure consistent performance across the entire fundraising portfolio, and work with our President and program leads to integrate new approaches effectively.
C&S Board Engagement. Partner with C&S’s well-connected board to strategically engage their networks for potential philanthropic relationships.

Work Environment, Salary, and Benefits
C&S is a remote workplace with staff across the country. We gather in person 2-3 times each year at our headquarters at the Carnegie Center in Princeton, NJ, for events that build trust and teamwork. Monthly regional and national travel is required to attend C&S convenings, field-wide conferences, and meetings with partners.
The budgeted salary range for this position is $250K – $275K with an outstanding benefits package including 22 days of PTO plus 12 days of sick leave, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans with FSA options, a 10% employer retirement contribution (with a 5% employee contribution), and more.
The C&S team is made up of educators, designers, researchers, strategists, project managers, and civic leaders. We value constant learning, belonging, gratitude, attentiveness, and a willingness to roll up our sleeves. Here, everyone has a role in shaping a strong and thriving America.

Qualifications
Demonstrated ability to establish credibility with people of significant wealth, including those whose wealth may be newly created, and build relationships across political, professional, and ideological differences.
Existing relationships or network connections among groups connected to emerging wealth (e.g., founders, investors, executives, family offices, wealth advisors, and those in venture or private capital or university major gifts advancement, etc.).
Skilled at understanding what motivates a potential partner and translating shared interests into opportunities for investment or partnership.
Experience advancing high-stakes relationships over time with an understanding of when and how to bring in other stakeholders to move a relationship forward.
Experience leading and developing small teams with a record of building a culture of trust, accountability, and high performance.

About the Institute for Citizens and Scholars
C&S sparks young people to create bold, fresh civic solutions that move our country forward. The mission of C&S is to cultivate talent, ideas, and networks that develop young people as effective, lifelong citizens. Our vision is a strong American democracy and a flourishing civil society where all people can thrive. We collaborate with leaders in higher education, business, and philanthropy to transform colleges, workplaces, and communities into hubs for civic development. In each of these spaces, we develop and implement programs that equip young people with the civic skills needed to address the divisive issues facing our country. Our offerings include co-designed programs, digital products, convenings, trainings, fellowships, and coalition networks – all with clear success metrics to measure real progress.

Upwardly Global (UpGlo) is a national nonprofit that helps immigrants, refugees, and asylees rebuild their professional careers in the United States. We work at both the direct service and system-change levels, building a more inclusive workforce and economy by ensuring everyone can fully use their skills and talents.

Here is what that means for a fundraiser:

The case for support is concrete and measurable. We can show a donor the economic return on a placed professional, not just a sentiment. That is a rare advantage in a first major gift conversation.
The prospect universe is genuinely underworked. Individual giving currently accounts for roughly $2M of our $14M in annual revenue. Our modeled major gift capacity is significantly larger, and whole segments of it (e.g., technology and finance executives, immigrant-founder networks, family foundations, DAF-advised households) have never been systematically cultivated at scale.
You will not be prospecting alone. Our CEO, CRO, Board, and program leadership actively open doors, and we fund prospect research, wealth screening, and Salesforce so your hours go to donor conversations rather than data archaeology.
The acquisition mandate is explicit. Bringing in new donors is the primary success measure for this role and is resourced and protected as such, not a stretch goal layered on top of a full stewardship load.

What Success Looks Like

We would rather be specific than aspirational. Targets will be finalized with you, but the shape of the role is:

First 90 days

Assess the existing pipeline and rate every prospect above $10K for capacity, inclination, and connection.
Build a qualification plan for 40 new prospects and complete your first 20 discovery visits.
Agree on a multi-year individual giving growth plan with the Chief Revenue Officer and CEO.

First 12 months

Personally close $2M from a portfolio of roughly 100–125 households, with at least 70% coming from donors new to UpGlo at the major gift level.
Move 20 new prospects into active cultivation and secure 10 six-figure commitments.
Make improvements to our current qualification engine in partnership with our Dev Ops team, ensuring repeatability, sourcing, research, discovery, and moves management that the team can run without you in the room.

By year three

Grow individual giving from $2M to $10M, with a materially more diversified donor base and a documented seven-figure prospect pipeline.

What You Will Own

New donor acquisition: the core of the role

Source, qualify, and convert new major donors at the $10K+ level, personally carrying relationships from discovery through close.
Design and run a disciplined prospecting engine: wealth screening, peer and Board referral, network mapping, event follow-up, DAF and family foundation research, and conversion of annual and mid-level donors.
Build re-engagement pathways for lapsed and dormant donors and upgrade paths for existing supporters with untapped capacity.
Partner with the CRO to set and hold the Individual Giving team's qualification standards: visits, moves, pipeline velocity; ensuring acquisition is never crowded out by renewal work.

Frontline fundraising

Manage a personal portfolio of high-net-worth donors and prospects, securing six- and seven-figure gifts.
Craft tailored solicitation strategies that connect each donor's motivation to UpGlo's program and policy work.
Represent UpGlo externally with authenticity, articulating our mission and results credibly to sophisticated audiences.

Strategy and team leadership

Partner with the CRO and lead the major gifts and individual giving program end to end: strategy, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Partner with the Director of Annual Giving and the Director of Stewardship to build one coherent donor journey from first gift to transformational commitment.
Build, supervise, and coach a team of gift officers and donor engagement staff, building a culture that rewards pipeline-building, not only renewal.
Work with our talented Development Operations team to ensure Salesforce, pipeline reporting, and forecasting remain genuinely useful for relationship management as we scale.
Collaborate with the CEO, Board, and leadership team to open new philanthropic networks, and with Finance, Communications, and Program teams to align priorities and impact storytelling.

Stewardship and engagement

Partner with the Director of Stewardship on the stewardship and recognition strategy that makes donors want to give again, and larger.
Help shape donor events, briefings, and campaigns that create qualification opportunities rather than one-off touchpoints.

Who We Are Looking For

Required

A documented record of acquiring new major donors, not only growing inherited portfolios. Be ready to walk us through relationships you sourced yourself, from first contact to close.
Personal closes at the six-figure level, with seven-figure experience or a credible path to it.
10+ years in nonprofit fundraising or comparable relationship-based revenue work, including 5+ years focused on major or individual giving.
Experience building a pipeline from thin inventory: prospect identification, qualification discipline, and moves management you designed rather than inherited.
Experience managing and developing frontline fundraisers, with evidence that your team's numbers improved under you.
Fluency with CRM-driven pipeline management and data-informed portfolio decisions (Salesforce NPSP preferred).
The judgment and presence to earn trust quickly with high-net-worth individuals, executives, and Board members.
Real interest in UpGlo's mission, and the ability to speak about immigration and economic mobility with nuance and care.

Helpful, not required

Campaign experience, particularly in the quiet phase.
Networks in technology, finance, immigrant-serving philanthropy, or family foundations.
Lived or professional experience with immigration, resettlement, or workforce development.

We evaluate candidates on demonstrated results rather than credentials. If you meet most of the above and can show the acquisition track record, please apply.

Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $135,000 – $145,000 depending on experience. We publish our banding and do not ask for salary history.
Health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement: 401(k) with employer match.
Time off: 160 hours PTO, 40 hours sick leave, 16 hours health and wellness time, your birthday off, and an organization-wide paid closure from December 24 through January 1.
Family: 12 weeks paid parental leave, gender inclusive.
Resourced to succeed: A dedicated travel and cultivation budget, prospect research and wealth screening tools, and a CEO and Board who show up for donor meetings.

How to Apply

Send your resume and a short note (a few paragraphs is plenty) about one major donor relationship you sourced and closed yourself: why you pursued them, how you got the first meeting, and what the gift became.

Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About The Department Of Natural Resources (DNR)

The Indiana Department of Natural Resources protects, enhances, preserves, and wisely uses natural, cultural, and recreational resources for the benefit of Indiana's citizens through professional leadership, management, and education.

Role Overview

Direct staff, funding, and and activities related to natural resources management in the division, including but not limited to management of invasive species, management of nuisance wildlife, reservoir crop lease management, wetland management, wildlife surveys, research, division training, and other natural resources related conservation activities.
Direct staff, funding, and activities related to cultural resources management in the division, including but not limited to coordination with DHPA for compliance with state and federal historic preservation laws, archaeological and historical research and education, division archives management, and division training.
Direct staff, funding, and activities related to interpretation of natural and cultural resources, facilities, and park operations in the division.This includes general day-to-day programming, special events, wayside signage, nature center exhibits and operations, interpretive planning, social media, brochures, and online resources related to the division and its facilities, services, programming, and history.
Direct staff, funding, and activities related to volunteers, friends groups, and a variety of other partnerships for the division.
Participate in budget planning, monitoring, and funding decisions for the Division.
Coordinate and communicate guidelines and actions related to the division's involvement and requirements with state, federal, or private grants.
Participate in personnel management for the division, including recruiting, hiring, training, retaining, performance management, disciplining, leadership development, and other aspects of human resources as needed, in particular when it relates to interpretive naturalists, assistant managers for wildlife, and other areas requiring expertise in the areas described above.
Direct the planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of web and social media efforts for the division (division level and properties).
Coordinate marketing efforts that drive revenue and expand experiences for the division in cooperation with Indiana State Park Inns, the DNR Division of Communications, other DNR Divisions as appropriate, and the Indiana Destination Development Corporation (IDDC).
Provide oversight of the site change process used to develop new facilities or modify existing ones on state park and reservoir properties, and participate in design and planning for facility improvements and new trails and other facilities.
Guide or participate in the planning for and review all publications, large-quantity distribution letters, newsletters, news releases, brochures, and social media campaigns prior to final publication and distribution.
Direct contracting for professional services, printed material, media services, and partnerships for the division, including video production, public opinion surveys, publication printing/distribution of materials, friends groups, exhibits, or in other needed areas.
Prepare written or oral public statements for department and division director and topical FAQs for significant changes or issues involving the division.
Facilitate the division's five-year strategic planning process, monitor and document completion of action items, and report on that progress to agency leadership and the public as appropriate.
Other duties as assigned.

Along with the Head of School, the Director of Advancement and External Affairs serves as the chief development officer and strategic advancement leader for Congressional, provides advice to the Head of School regarding fundraising priorities, and leads the advancement team. In addition to formal duties, the successful director of advancement and external affairs must be an integral member of the school community and take an active interest in the social and community-building activities of the school.

Develops the annual advancement plan, providing counsel and working in concert with the Head of School and current Strategic Plan
Develops a culture of philanthropy at the School, fostering good will with constituents at every level, cultivates connections with the School community, and develops new relations with those outside the School
Works in concert with the Head of School in identifying, cultivating, and soliciting a portfolio of major donors, including donors making planned gifts to the School
Devises and manages a fundraising program to attract maximum gift support through an annual fund, planned giving, corporate and foundation grants, and endowment giving
Develops, implements and manages the annual giving program
Develops and maintains strategic partnerships with key business, community, academic and philanthropic organizations
Identifies opportunities to increase the visibility of Congressional School among AISGW, VAIS and NAIS schools, and build the School's reputation and presence as a mission-driven, engaged, strong community player and employer
Develops, implements and manages a strong alumni base with a goal toward increasing fundraising initiatives
Works in concert with the Head of School to develop and manage a major gifts program, and partners with Head of School in cultivating and soliciting major gifts
Designs, organizes, manages, and implements all capital and endowment campaigns
Identifies and solicits corporate and foundation grants
Serves as a member of the School's Leadership Team
Develops an annual budget that is directly linked to the priorities of the department and the institution and works with the CFO/COO to ensure prudent budget expenses
Supervises, sets direction and supports goals for the Advancement team (consisting of the Advancement Accociate) in order to maximize their individual talents and encourage professional growth

A sense of humor, warm personality, and growth-mindset

new_jobs.description:
About ASG

ASG is a New York–headquartered, SEC-registered investment firm with approximately $1.8 billion in assets under management. The firm invests in global innovation across public and private markets, applying institutional-grade rigor, disciplined underwriting, and proprietary data intelligence to identify and invest in category-defining companies.

Role Summary

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the firm’s organizational anchor. This role most deeply embedded across every function, and the force that transforms the CEO’s vision into a platform capable of sustained, compounding growth.
As AUM scales, organizational complexity is inevitable. The COO’s core mandate is to ensure that structure is always ahead of scale: that governance is codified rather than assumed, that systems are more reliable than any individual, and that the platform is architected to support multiple funds and strategies over the long term.
The COO is accountable for three interconnected layers of value creation:
Designing the organizational and governance architecture that enables the firm to grow without losing cohesion;
Building the systems and process infrastructure that turns institutional experience into repeatable, scalable capability; and
Laying the platform foundation that gives the firm compounding structural advantages as it expands.

The COO is the firm’s connective tissue. The stronger and more integrated that tissue, the more efficiently the entire organization performs.

Core Responsibilities

I. Organizational Governance & Structural Design

1. Three-Engine Clarity: Investment | Finance & Risk | Platform

Define authority boundaries, accountability frameworks, and KPIs across Investment, Finance & Risk, and Platform, formally documented in policy and performance structures.
Maintain clean ownership separation while enabling structured cross-engine coordination.
Audit engine effectiveness as the firm grows and adjust governance design proactively.

2. Layered Decision Architecture

Own and optimize the firm's formal governance bodies (IC, Portfolio Review, Operating Committee, Risk & Valuation Committee), ensuring each addresses the right decision tier.
Design escalation paths, pre-meeting preparation standards, and post-meeting accountability mechanisms.
Establish the firm's weekly, monthly, and quarterly operating cadence as a structured rhythm.

3. Modular Organizational Build-Out

Build functional infrastructure around scoped modules (Fund Ops, IR Ops, Portfolio Ops, Operational Systems, Risk & Compliance), each with defined ownership, deliverables, KPIs, and hiring roadmap.
Partner with HR on headcount planning, role design, and leadership development.
Reinforce firm-wide performance management and accountability norms.

II. Systems, Process & Institutional Infrastructure

1. Single Source of Truth

Lead unification of CRM, Portfolio Management, Fund Administration, and Document Management into a consistent operational data layer.
Establish data governance standards; eliminate version conflicts and shadow tracking.
Select and manage technology vendors against defined SLAs.

2. Risk Control Embedded in Process

Design risk controls into workflows as structural safeguards, not compliance afterthoughts.
Implement access permissions, information barriers, vendor risk management, and key-person mitigation.
Ensure Risk & Compliance has codified integration points within Investment, Finance, and IR workflows.

3. Standardized Playbooks & Institutional Memory

Develop replicable playbooks for core workflows (investment process, QBR, LP DD, LP engagement, crisis management).
Capture institutional knowledge in transferable, maintained systems.
stablish documentation standards; treat playbooks as living documents.

4. Critical Path Optimization & Automation

Eliminate friction in high-frequency workflows (legal execution, KYC, fund administration, capital calls) through SOP redesign, tooling, or restructured ownership.
Prioritize automation to compress cycle times and reduce manual handoffs.
Track cycle time reduction as a core performance metric.

III. Platform Scalability & Long-Term Capability

1. Modular Platform Expansion

Ensure each operational module has defined objectives, measurable outputs, KPIs, and a dedicated budget.
Build shared infrastructure to be strategy-agnostic (VC, Growth, PE, Credit) while investment decision-making remains independent.
Resource operational capacity ahead of AUM growth and fund launch milestones.

2. Budget as Capability Investment

Evaluate infrastructure and vendor investments through an explicit ROI framework focused on long-term capability gain.
Set clear boundaries between self-build, licensed software, and outsourced service models.
Maintain a multi-year operational investment roadmap.

3. Multi-Strategy Shared Platform

Architect the platform so new fund vintages, asset classes, or geographies add incremental, not exponential, operational complexity.
Maintain separation between the platform layer and the investment decision layer.
Build integration standards so new strategies can be onboarded with speed and consistency.

4. Incentive Structure & Long-Term Alignment

Collaborate with the CEO and HR on a compensation framework tied to long-term platform health.
Structure incentive triggers around organizational, system, AUM, and operational efficiency milestones rather than solely deal outcomes.

Required Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in operations, infrastructure, or general management at SEC-registered investment firms, asset managers, hedge funds, institutional financial services firms, or high-growth companies.
Demonstrated track record of building or scaling operational platforms, systems, and teams through periods of rapid growth.
Familiarity with the operational infrastructure supporting investment firms, including fund administration, portfolio management systems, CRM platforms, document management, and risk infrastructure, or demonstrated ability to build comparable systems in another context.
Working knowledge of SEC, RIA, and broader regulatory frameworks applicable to U.S. investment advisers.
Proven experience designing governance structures, decision forums, and operating cadences in growing organizations.
Strong systems thinking, ability to translate strategy into documented, scalable processes.
Sound judgment in vendor selection, technology investment, and build-vs-buy decisions.
Outstanding written communication and documentation discipline.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience as a founder, CEO, or COO of a startup or high-growth company, particularly those who have built operating structure, systems, and teams from an early stage.
Prior COO, Head of Operations, or Chief of Staff experience at an investment firm with AUM growth across multiple fund vintages.
Exposure to both public and private market investment operations.
MBA, JD, CPA, or equivalent advanced credential.
Experience supporting multi-jurisdictional operations (including Asia).

Reporting & Scope

Reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer.
Operates as a senior individual contributor and firm-wide platform architect, working through governance forums, functional partnerships, and CEO-delegated authority. The role does not have direct reports at this time; team build-out under the COO’s scope will be considered as the firm scales.
Sits on or chairs the firm’s principal governance committees as designed.

What We Offer

The opportunity to architect the operational foundation of a growing, SEC-registered investment platform.
High-impact role with direct CEO partnership and meaningful influence across firm strategy.
Competitive compensation, including base, performance bonus, and long-term incentive structure tied to platform health.

25 years in, Upwardly Global (UpGlo) has a proven program, a compelling case for support, and a major donor base that is far smaller than that case warrants. We are hiring a major gifts leader to change that, primarily by finding, qualifying, and closing donors who do not know us yet.
This is a build role, not a maintenance role. If your best work has been opening new relationships rather than inheriting mature ones, keep reading.

Why This Role, Why Now

Upwardly Global (UpGlo) is a national nonprofit that helps immigrants, refugees, and asylees rebuild their professional careers in the United States. We work at both the direct service and system-change levels, building a more inclusive workforce and economy by ensuring everyone can fully use their skills and talents.

Here is what that means for a fundraiser:

The case for support is concrete and measurable. We can show a donor the economic return on a placed professional, not just a sentiment. That is a rare advantage in a first major gift conversation.
The prospect universe is genuinely underworked. Individual giving currently accounts for roughly $2M of our $14M in annual revenue. Our modeled major gift capacity is significantly larger, and whole segments of it (e.g., technology and finance executives, immigrant-founder networks, family foundations, DAF-advised households) have never been systematically cultivated at scale.
You will not be prospecting alone. Our CEO, CRO, Board, and program leadership actively open doors, and we fund prospect research, wealth screening, and Salesforce so your hours go to donor conversations rather than data archaeology.
The acquisition mandate is explicit. Bringing in new donors is the primary success measure for this role and is resourced and protected as such, not a stretch goal layered on top of a full stewardship load.

What Success Looks Like

We would rather be specific than aspirational. Targets will be finalized with you, but the shape of the role is:

First 90 days

Assess the existing pipeline and rate every prospect above $10K for capacity, inclination, and connection.
Build a qualification plan for 40 new prospects and complete your first 20 discovery visits.
Agree on a multi-year individual giving growth plan with the Chief Revenue Officer and CEO.

First 12 months

Personally close $2M from a portfolio of roughly 100–125 households, with at least 70% coming from donors new to UpGlo at the major gift level.
Move 20 new prospects into active cultivation and secure 10 six-figure commitments.
Make improvements to our current qualification engine in partnership with our Dev Ops team, ensuring repeatability, sourcing, research, discovery, and moves management that the team can run without you in the room.

By year three

Grow individual giving from $2M to $10M, with a materially more diversified donor base and a documented seven-figure prospect pipeline.

What You Will Own

New donor acquisition: the core of the role

Source, qualify, and convert new major donors at the $10K+ level, personally carrying relationships from discovery through close.
Design and run a disciplined prospecting engine: wealth screening, peer and Board referral, network mapping, event follow-up, DAF and family foundation research, and conversion of annual and mid-level donors.
Build re-engagement pathways for lapsed and dormant donors and upgrade paths for existing supporters with untapped capacity.
Partner with the CRO to set and hold the Individual Giving team's qualification standards: visits, moves, pipeline velocity; ensuring acquisition is never crowded out by renewal work.

Frontline fundraising

Manage a personal portfolio of high-net-worth donors and prospects, securing six- and seven-figure gifts.
Craft tailored solicitation strategies that connect each donor's motivation to UpGlo's program and policy work.
Represent UpGlo externally with authenticity, articulating our mission and results credibly to sophisticated audiences.

Strategy and team leadership

Partner with the CRO and lead the major gifts and individual giving program end to end: strategy, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Partner with the Director of Annual Giving and the Director of Stewardship to build one coherent donor journey from first gift to transformational commitment.
Build, supervise, and coach a team of gift officers and donor engagement staff, building a culture that rewards pipeline-building, not only renewal.
Work with our talented Development Operations team to ensure Salesforce, pipeline reporting, and forecasting remain genuinely useful for relationship management as we scale.
Collaborate with the CEO, Board, and leadership team to open new philanthropic networks, and with Finance, Communications, and Program teams to align priorities and impact storytelling.

Stewardship and engagement

Partner with the Director of Stewardship on the stewardship and recognition strategy that makes donors want to give again, and larger.
Help shape donor events, briefings, and campaigns that create qualification opportunities rather than one-off touchpoints.

Who We Are Looking For

Required

A documented record of acquiring new major donors, not only growing inherited portfolios. Be ready to walk us through relationships you sourced yourself, from first contact to close.
Personal closes at the six-figure level, with seven-figure experience or a credible path to it.
10+ years in nonprofit fundraising or comparable relationship-based revenue work, including 5+ years focused on major or individual giving.
Experience building a pipeline from thin inventory: prospect identification, qualification discipline, and moves management you designed rather than inherited.
Experience managing and developing frontline fundraisers, with evidence that your team's numbers improved under you.
Fluency with CRM-driven pipeline management and data-informed portfolio decisions (Salesforce NPSP preferred).
The judgment and presence to earn trust quickly with high-net-worth individuals, executives, and Board members.
Real interest in UpGlo's mission, and the ability to speak about immigration and economic mobility with nuance and care.

Helpful, not required

Campaign experience, particularly in the quiet phase.
Networks in technology, finance, immigrant-serving philanthropy, or family foundations.
Lived or professional experience with immigration, resettlement, or workforce development.

We evaluate candidates on demonstrated results rather than credentials. If you meet most of the above and can show the acquisition track record, please apply.

Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $135,000 – $145,000 depending on experience. We publish our banding and do not ask for salary history.
Health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement: 401(k) with employer match.
Time off: 160 hours PTO, 40 hours sick leave, 16 hours health and wellness time, your birthday off, and an organization-wide paid closure from December 24 through January 1.
Family: 12 weeks paid parental leave, gender inclusive.
Resourced to succeed: A dedicated travel and cultivation budget, prospect research and wealth screening tools, and a CEO and Board who show up for donor meetings.

How to Apply

Send your resume and a short note (a few paragraphs is plenty) about one major donor relationship you sourced and closed yourself: why you pursued them, how you got the first meeting, and what the gift became.

Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About The Department Of Natural Resources (DNR)

The Indiana Department of Natural Resources protects, enhances, preserves, and wisely uses natural, cultural, and recreational resources for the benefit of Indiana's citizens through professional leadership, management, and education.

Role Overview

Direct staff, funding, and and activities related to natural resources management in the division, including but not limited to management of invasive species, management of nuisance wildlife, reservoir crop lease management, wetland management, wildlife surveys, research, division training, and other natural resources related conservation activities.
Direct staff, funding, and activities related to cultural resources management in the division, including but not limited to coordination with DHPA for compliance with state and federal historic preservation laws, archaeological and historical research and education, division archives management, and division training.
Direct staff, funding, and activities related to interpretation of natural and cultural resources, facilities, and park operations in the division.This includes general day-to-day programming, special events, wayside signage, nature center exhibits and operations, interpretive planning, social media, brochures, and online resources related to the division and its facilities, services, programming, and history.
Direct staff, funding, and activities related to volunteers, friends groups, and a variety of other partnerships for the division.
Participate in budget planning, monitoring, and funding decisions for the Division.
Coordinate and communicate guidelines and actions related to the division's involvement and requirements with state, federal, or private grants.
Participate in personnel management for the division, including recruiting, hiring, training, retaining, performance management, disciplining, leadership development, and other aspects of human resources as needed, in particular when it relates to interpretive naturalists, assistant managers for wildlife, and other areas requiring expertise in the areas described above.
Direct the planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of web and social media efforts for the division (division level and properties).
Coordinate marketing efforts that drive revenue and expand experiences for the division in cooperation with Indiana State Park Inns, the DNR Division of Communications, other DNR Divisions as appropriate, and the Indiana Destination Development Corporation (IDDC).
Provide oversight of the site change process used to develop new facilities or modify existing ones on state park and reservoir properties, and participate in design and planning for facility improvements and new trails and other facilities.
Guide or participate in the planning for and review all publications, large-quantity distribution letters, newsletters, news releases, brochures, and social media campaigns prior to final publication and distribution.
Direct contracting for professional services, printed material, media services, and partnerships for the division, including video production, public opinion surveys, publication printing/distribution of materials, friends groups, exhibits, or in other needed areas.
Prepare written or oral public statements for department and division director and topical FAQs for significant changes or issues involving the division.
Facilitate the division's five-year strategic planning process, monitor and document completion of action items, and report on that progress to agency leadership and the public as appropriate.
Other duties as assigned.

Along with the Head of School, the Director of Advancement and External Affairs serves as the chief development officer and strategic advancement leader for Congressional, provides advice to the Head of School regarding fundraising priorities, and leads the advancement team. In addition to formal duties, the successful director of advancement and external affairs must be an integral member of the school community and take an active interest in the social and community-building activities of the school.

Develops the annual advancement plan, providing counsel and working in concert with the Head of School and current Strategic Plan
Develops a culture of philanthropy at the School, fostering good will with constituents at every level, cultivates connections with the School community, and develops new relations with those outside the School
Works in concert with the Head of School in identifying, cultivating, and soliciting a portfolio of major donors, including donors making planned gifts to the School
Devises and manages a fundraising program to attract maximum gift support through an annual fund, planned giving, corporate and foundation grants, and endowment giving
Develops, implements and manages the annual giving program
Develops and maintains strategic partnerships with key business, community, academic and philanthropic organizations
Identifies opportunities to increase the visibility of Congressional School among AISGW, VAIS and NAIS schools, and build the School's reputation and presence as a mission-driven, engaged, strong community player and employer
Develops, implements and manages a strong alumni base with a goal toward increasing fundraising initiatives
Works in concert with the Head of School to develop and manage a major gifts program, and partners with Head of School in cultivating and soliciting major gifts
Designs, organizes, manages, and implements all capital and endowment campaigns
Identifies and solicits corporate and foundation grants
Serves as a member of the School's Leadership Team
Develops an annual budget that is directly linked to the priorities of the department and the institution and works with the CFO/COO to ensure prudent budget expenses
Supervises, sets direction and supports goals for the Advancement team (consisting of the Advancement Accociate) in order to maximize their individual talents and encourage professional growth
Assists the Director of Strategic Marketing and Communications with the planning and implementation of the School's long-range marketing plan

Maintains a regular presence in the School community
Performs other initiatives, special programs and duties as assigned by the Head of School

Ease in working with donors, parents, board members, community members and other stakeholders and can work independently
Broad and deep knowledge of fundraising, communications, and marketing, and the ways in which these three functional areas must integrate seamlessly in order to form a successful, comprehensive advancement effort

A sense of humor, warm personality, and growth-mindset
